---
title: "Experimental shared-content storage"
---

<!-- VERIFIED_RELEASE_STATUS -->
This guide accompanies the experimental preview.5 candidate. Final publication
and installation are still pending. Keep an independent backup.

Use Xet when large changed files share repeated pieces of bytes. Choose ordinary
backups or [whole-file sharing](cas-github.qmd) when chunk sharing is unnecessary.
The helper is optional and separate from the CLI and R package.

Files are split into reusable pieces by the optional upstream Xet helper. This may
save storage when large files share uncompressed bytes. Already-compressed files
may benefit little. Synthetic results do not predict savings for real datasets.

Both local and GitHub destinations use structure: xet.
GitHub transports this same local engine/store as a complete ZIP, not a hosted
Xet service. One long-running storage release holds it. No incremental pack transport or automatic migration is implemented. Tests use
synthetic bytes; existing user datasets are not uploaded by the test workflow.

## Install the optional helper

The helper is qualified on Linux/WSL. A macOS helper has not been qualified;
native Windows Xet execution is rejected. Other storage backends remain available
on Windows. The normal CLI download needs no Rust compiler, but building this
optional helper needs Python 3, Git, a native C/C++ compiler/linker and CMake,
Rust/Cargo 1.95.0 with Clippy, and network
access to pinned source and locked registry dependencies.

From the matching projcli source checkout:

```sh
rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --component clippy
work=$(mktemp -d)
python3 tools/xet-engine/build.py \
  --source "$work/upstream" \
  --output "$HOME/.local/bin/proj-xet-engine"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
proj-xet-engine info
```

The source directory must not already exist. This substantial optional build
fetches the exact upstream pin into that disposable directory, checks Cargo.lock,
builds and lints the helper, and writes provenance beside it. It does not modify
the original projr checkout or require a Hugging Face account/server. Keep the
provenance with your store; no automatic helper upgrade occurs.

## Choose the storage options

| Setting | Current support |
|---|---|
| Provider | local or github; both use the same local helper |
| structure | xet |
| manifest | auto or remote: full records in the store, small references in the project |
| manifest-style | tree |
| manifest-format | Fixed JSON binding; flat/CSV/dictionary overrides are rejected |
| content / build.dest content | Declared logical folders; destination selection can narrow the set |

Local and GitHub examples below archive existing raw-data with scripts: [] and
Git disabled. Use explicit paths and an existing VERSION file. Preview first;
the production build updates version and saves selected data:

```sh
proj build-dev
proj build --patch
```

Since these examples disable Git integration, commit .proj/remotes references alongside VERSION/configuration
yourself if you need recovery from a future checkout. Removing a destination
from build.dest stops uploads without removing restore access.

## Why this remains experimental

Upstream's [local client is a testing/development backend](https://github.com/huggingface/xet-core/blob/629562cd9fc37432317eb57811faf13a6935c601/xet_client/src/cas_client/simulation/mod.rs).
Its [README directs ordinary use through huggingface_hub](https://github.com/huggingface/xet-core/blob/629562cd9fc37432317eb57811faf13a6935c601/README.md).
Apache-2.0 permits reuse but does not establish an archival compatibility/support
promise. The helper requires the exact tested upstream revision and unknown
formats fail; upgrading must not silently reinterpret stored data.

[Restart tests](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/40459341098)
passed. [Interruption/export qualification](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/40463702593)
passed selected process interruption/retry and stopped-writer ZIP export/import,
but failed corruption detection: the default upstream local download returned
success with wrong bytes. Unfinished reads also panicked. Those failures remain
recorded. The new core independently checks reconstructed length/BLAKE3 in private
staging before using the existing guarded destination installer.

A cooperative claim serializes one project's store operations, including reads
which can mutate upstream caches. Finalized verified content precedes immutable
snapshot references. No persistent full-file copy is kept, but ingest/restore
needs temporary disk space. Sparse database allocation can grow on export/import.
A stale claim fails closed; no automatic stale-lock removal or migration occurs.

Snapshots reuse the existing complete file inventory and pure directory identities.
A backend-specific binding maps whole-file digests to upstream reconstruction
addresses. File digests, directory roots, version metadata and Xet IDs stay distinct.
Legacy CAS IDs/readers are untouched.

The dedicated remote integration gate checks exact recovery and complete destination preservation; see the draft PR's exact-head results. These checks do not establish long-term archival support. Unix runtime only until equivalent
hard-link validation is implemented on Windows. No power-loss, concurrent hot-copy,
arbitrary interruption-point or production-readiness guarantee follows. Reusing
upstream chunk/hash/codec primitives with a proj-owned durable backend is another
route, but requires real persistence/index/recovery engineering.

## Save a local copy

Use the matching CLI and helper; no automatic helper installation occurs.
The separately built pinned helper must already be on PATH as proj-xet-engine.
No build/init/query automatically installs it or logs into Hugging Face.
Current runtime support is Unix; Windows proj still works with ordinary backends.

For a project that only archives existing data, an explicit empty script list
avoids rerunning an analysis:

```yaml
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: raw-data
  cache:
    path: cache
    safe: true
remotes:
  local:
    shared-content:
      path: ../experimental-store
      structure: xet
      content: [raw-data]
build:
  scripts: []
  git: false
  dest:
    shared-content: {}
```

A production build stores selected folders; preview does not upload, require the
helper or update backend caches. Queries never activate writes. Removing the
remote from build.dest stops uploads while preserving explicit recovery lookup.
Optional build.dest content narrows the remote's eligible labels.

After finalization/independent byte verification, the build saves a complete store
snapshot and small project reference under .proj/remotes. The reference's snapshot
field supplies the exact ID:

```sh
proj remote verify --title shared-content --snapshot SNAPSHOT_ID
proj remote restore --title shared-content --snapshot SNAPSHOT_ID --label raw-data --clear
```

Restore uses the label's configured final directory. Without --clear, extra
destination files survive; with it, membership matches the snapshot. Both paths
verify private reconstructed bytes before replacement. Verify/restore take the
store claim and can update backend caches; they are not byte-for-byte read-only
store operations. They leave project VERSION unchanged and need no old project CSV.

Initial configured support is remote full metadata (manifest auto/remote), tree
identities and JSON binding. Project/both, flat/CSV/dictionary overrides fail
preflight rather than being ignored. Root manifest.csv and old ordinary/CAS
formats remain unchanged. Broader format parity is not implemented. GitHub transfer uses this same engine through the complete-store transport described below.

Experimental Xet preview does not copy/restore mutable engine stores under the
project-only claim. It never opens the engine, even with an existing busy store.
Arbitrary script/hook store edits are outside that preview guarantee. Every
production target's types/format are checked before hooks, independently of
one-time helper discovery. The configured integration gate covers multiple targets and busy-store handling.

## How the complete store is transferred

The transport prepares the same local store for complete ZIP
transfer. It takes the cooperative store claim while copying stopped-writer
persistent data, excludes client caches and writer claims, and validates every
committed version using the pinned helper. A separate export manifest records
exact file paths, byte lengths and BLAKE3 digests. Unknown store files fail rather
than disappearing silently. This is a full-history copy, including orphan packs;
it does not reclaim space.

Import first checks the trusted ZIP digest and byte length, then bounded safe
extraction, exact file membership, and independent reconstruction of every
committed snapshot in a fresh private tree. It never replaces an existing store.
Keep the ZIP digest in trusted project/reference metadata; an internal checksum
alone does not authenticate an archive.

Configured GitHub publication uses this same transport.
Engine and mocked-transport tests passed; final real GitHub evidence is recorded separately. Sparse databases can consume more temporary
disk space than their allocated size in the original store. No live-copy or
system power-loss guarantee is claimed.

## GitHub transfer and failed uploads

One long-running storage release can hold complete ZIPs of the same local store.
The source library uploads a uniquely named ZIP without deleting the previous
one, downloads it again, and checks both transport bytes and every stored version
before returning a reference. The project must save that reference only after
success. A failed or interrupted upload can leave an unreferenced ZIP; the
previous reference and export remain available.

Recovery starts from a trusted explicit project reference. The downloaded ZIP
opens as a fresh private local store, so adding a version uses exactly the same
engine as local storage. The updated complete store is then exported again.
GitHub does not run a Xet service, and this initial design transfers the entire
ZIP rather than only changed pieces.

There is no automatic latest-export lookup, shared remote writer
coordination or cleanup policy. Local engine operations retain their cooperative
writer claim. Independent writers can leave separate immutable exports; callers
must not silently choose one or claim a merged history. Configured builds use the Git-tracked locators described below.

Complete exports accumulate until an explicit future retention policy is chosen.
No automatic deletion is performed. GitHub's per-asset limit is below 2 GiB; this
client rejects larger exports before upload. Temporary expanded database copies
can be much larger than the compressed ZIP. Tests use only a loopback mock REST
service and synthetic bytes, not a live GitHub data release.

## Keep the store on GitHub

The same local engine and structure selector apply:

```yaml
directories:
  raw-data:
    path: raw-data
  cache:
    path: cache
    safe: true
  output:
    path: output
remotes:
  github:
    project-data-store:
      structure: xet
      content: [raw-data]
build:
  scripts: []
  git: false
  dest:
    project-data-store: {}
```

The remote name selects one long-running storage release. The repository comes
from the project's Git origin. Existing GitHub authentication is used; no account,
token, engine or R package is installed automatically. Keep credentials out of YAML.
The optional pinned engine is required for production only. Preview and queries
do not open the engine or contact the release.

Each upload is downloaded and fully checked before writing project metadata under
.proj/remotes/<remote-name-hash>/xet-github/v1/. The file current.json selects the
trusted store for the next build; immutable snapshots/<first2>/<rest>.json locators
retain each earlier snapshot's exact ZIP. Each binds repository, API origin, tag,
ZIP name/digest/length, backend/upstream and included snapshot IDs.
Keep these files in project Git history. Config relocation must not silently
reinterpret old locators; explicit migration is required.

Recover the exact snapshot ID from the project's locator, then:

```sh
proj remote restore --provider github --title project-data-store \
  --snapshot SNAPSHOT_ID --label raw-data --clear \
  --max-bytes 1073741824 --max-expanded-bytes 4294967296

proj remote verify --title project-data-store --snapshot SNAPSHOT_ID \
  --max-bytes 1073741824 --max-expanded-bytes 4294967296
```

A fresh checkout needs its trusted locators, config, existing authentication and
pinned engine. It needs no previous local store, caches, root CSV or current upload
selection. If locators are lost, recover them from project Git history instead of
guessing by hash or upload time. Full manifests remain in exports; automatic
remote-only locator recovery is not implemented.

Production caps ZIPs below 2 GiB and expanded stores at 8 GiB; explicit recovery
requires caller-selected budgets. Bounds are not disk reservations. Temporary
copies can need much more space than the original sparse database. Every update
transfers the complete ZIP; retaining old ZIPs also repeats history on GitHub.
Previous exports and failed/orphan uploads remain:
there is no automatic retention cleanup, and GitHub asset quotas still apply.

One project uses each store. Project writer exclusion and immutable exports protect
local operations and old bytes, but there is no distributed linear-head protocol.
Concurrent checkouts can create separate exports and conflicting Git locators;
there is no automatic multi-machine history merge.

Xet still repeats a complete readable inventory and file-address binding for each
version. Shared directory identities and engine chunk deduplication do not imply
version-level inventory deduplication.
